answer: A bridge between identity and stake can stop Sybil floods: every agent must lock a deposit at a single verified vertex of a trust graph before it may trade, and each new identity it spawns splits that same deposit instead of adding fresh credit. Forging a thousand sock puppets then costs a thousand deposits, while honest agents earn fees as their vertex rises toward the zenith of the reputation ranking. An attacker pays linearly per fake identity and gains nothing extra, so mass fakery becomes unprofitable.
